items.title: Vinesh Phogat case: Delhi HC says WFI must balance interests of nation and women athletes returning after childbirth
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday remarked that the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) must come up with guidelines to enable participation of female athletes returning after maternity leave. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said that a balance must be struck between the interests of the country and the athlete. The Court made the remark while hearing Olympian Vinesh Phogat’s plea seeking directions to allow her to participate in the trials for the Senior World Wrestling Championship scheduled on September 14. Senior Advocate Rajshekhar Rao appeared for Phogat and told the Bench that the WFI has displayed “absolute arbitrariness” in the case and she was informed of the selection criteria only on September 7. “Effectively, it means I am out of reckoning for two more years and I am finished as an athlete,” he said. The counsel appearing for the WFI told the Bench that Phogat has not been banned from participation. He said that the medal winners from 2025 and 2026 are eligible for selection for this year’s World Championship and Phogat can participate at the state and national levels and make her way up. items.title: Delhi High Court denies Vinesh Phogat interim relief to participate in World Wrestling Championships trials
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday declined to grant wrestler Vinesh Phogat interim relief to participate in the selection trials for the 2026 Senior World Wrestling Championships starting on September 14. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said that the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) for the World Wrestling Championships could not be relaxed exclusively in Phogat’s favour at the interim stage. “The interest of the country in ensuring that its representatives are selected through a fair, uniform and performance- based process is of paramount importance. At this interim stage, therefore, this Court is of the view that the eligibility criteria applicable to all athletes ought not to be relaxed in favour of the petitioner alone, particularly when such relaxation may have consequences for other similarly situated athletes who are not before this Court,” the Court observed. The World Championships will take place in Kazakhstan's Astana from October 24 to November 1. items.title: Teacher hitting girl students on back, waist without sexual intent not offence under POCSO Act: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has recently quashed a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) against a school teacher accused of hitting minor girl students on their back and waist during class [Bhaskar Paul v. State of West Bengal]. In an order passed on September 8, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held that the students’ statements did not indicate that the teacher had touched them with sexual intent, which is necessary to constitute sexual assault under the POCSO Act. The Court acknowledged that the teacher’s use of corporal punishment was inappropriate and that he should have been more sensitive while dealing with girl students. However, it said that such conduct alone could not justify prosecuting him for aggravated sexual assault under the POCSO Act. items.title: Courts must protect poor to preserve India's socialist goal in Constitution: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently stressed that courts must ensure the protection of rights of weaker sections of the society to preserve the ‘socialist’ structure of India envisaged in the preamble of the Constitution.[ Union of India and Ors Vs Mithai Lal and Ors ]. The Division Bench of Justice C Hari Shankar and Justice Om Prakash Shukla made these observations in a matter concerning regularisation of the vendors engaged by Indian Railways. “It is time that Courts protected the interests of the weaker sections of the society and persons drawing paltry wages, so as to ensure that the socialist structure of our democracy – which is a preambular goal – remains intact,” the Court said in a judgement delivered on September 8. The petitioner-vendors had initially been engaged on a commission basis by the Railways. After years of service, they moved the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) claiming regularisation of their services in Railways. In a 2016 order, the CAT directed Railways to regularise the services of the vendors within 90 days along with allowances and cost of litigation. items.title: Bombay HC laments IIT Bombay's 13-year-old patent dispute over scientist's life-saving invention
items.summary: In a patent battle pending for over a decade in relation to a crucial biomedical invention, the Bombay High Court has ruled in favour of an Indian scientist and against the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay [Tarkeshwar Chandrakant Patil v. IIT, Bombay & Ors] Justice Somasekhar Sundaresan declared Dr Tarkeshwar Chandrakant Patil as the original inventor of the patent and directed a Deputy Controller of Patents and Designs to recognize him as the applicant in a patent application filed by IIT Bombay (IITB) in 2013. The Court ruled that IIT Bombay could not have pursued the patent application on its own after it executed a worldwide assignment deed in July 2017 to transfer to Patil the full and exclusive right, title and interest in the invention. The Court rejected the argument that the deed of assignment did not extend to India but only to the United States. It, thus, ordered the Controller to process the patent application, with Patil as the applicant. items.title: Kerala High Court sets 2-week deadline for its judges to decide bail petitions
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has set time limits for adjudication of regular and anticipatory bail applications filed before the High Court by accused in criminal cases. According to a notice issued on September 10, the Chief Justice has set an upper time limit of 2 weeks to dispose of regular bail applications. Time granted for counsel to get instructions in regular bail matters shall not be allowed to exceed 7 working days. For anticipatory bail applications, the maximum time for disposal has been set at 6 weeks. The notice was issued in line with the Supreme Court's May 11 order which directed High Courts to take steps to speed up bail hearings. items.title: Delhi High Court slams Punjab & Sind Bank for denying reward to manager who foiled robbery in 1998
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently directed the Punjab & Sind Bank to pay an amount of ₹50,000, along with an annual interest of 12 percent, to a manager who had foiled a robbery attempt at its Najafgarh Branch in 1998 [ Surjit Singh Vs Punjab & Sind Bank] . Justice Neena Bansal Krishna also awarded litigation costs of ₹2 lakh to the manager, Surjit Singh, while taking exception to the management’s conduct of making him suffer litigation for 28 years over compensation for his bravery. The Court said that instead of the bank and the government itself rewarding Singh in accordance with the relevant guidelines, they added insult to injury by asserting that his act was not covered by the guidelines. "Such conduct is not becoming of the Bank, which itself, in fact, should have rewarded and acknowledged the Petitioner for his exemplary conduct, rather than driving him to seek reward to which he was entitled. It has taken him since 28 years to get the validation of his act," the Court said. The Court added that the question was not of money but of the honour, which should have come to him on its own without litigation. items.title: No offence of rape on promise of marriage when victim and accused already married to other people: HP High Court
items.summary: The Himachal Pradesh High Court recently held that a promise of marriage may not amount to the offence of deceitful sexual intercourse when both the accused and the victim are already married to other people and were aware of each other’s marital status [Vinod Kumar v State of Himachal Pradesh] . Justice Sandeep Sharma made the observation while granting bail to one Vinod Kumar, an astrologer, accused of sexually assaulting a 31-year-old woman on the alleged promise of marriage. In the order dated September 3, the Court noted that both the accused and the woman were married to other people and neither had divorced their respective spouses. It therefore found that there was prima facie no question of a promise to marry. "There was no question of promise to marry, especially when factum of marriage of the petitioner as well victim/prosecutrix was in the know of the victim/prosecutrix as well as bail petitioner. Once victim/prosecutrix as well as petitioner had not taken divorce from their respective spouses, they otherwise could not have solemnize marriage," held the Court. items.title: Mumbai court grants bail to TISS student arrested for slogans supporting Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
items.summary: A Mumbai court has granted bail to Abhirup Ashim Paul, a student of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), who was arrested for allegedly raising slogans supporting jailed activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. [Abhirup Paul v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.] Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Dattatray Shankarrao Khedekar observed that Paul had already undergone custodial interrogation for sufficient period. Pertinently, the Court also said that there was no evidence linking him to any Maoist or any other banned organisation. “Prima facie except suspicion, there is no material to link the activities of the accused with mind set of maoist or against the nation or associating with banned organization against India,” the judge noted. The Court observed that having soft copies of the Maoist books and raising campus slogans in support of jailed activists did not amount to anti-national activity and an inference of being a Moaist cannot be drawn from the same. "Merely because of finding of pdf books (on Maoism), the inference of connection with the mind set of maoist can not be draw," the Court ruled. items.title: Kerala HC orders Meta to block video containing derogatory remarks on Sabarimala deities
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday directed Meta to temporarily block public access to a social media video containing scandalous and indecent remarks against Sabarimala deities [Rahul K Easwar v State of Kerala & ors]. Justice G Girish passed the interim order on a plea filed by right-wing activist and public commentator Rahul K Easwar who moved the Court seeking removal of the video and action against the Dalit activist Sunny M Kapikad who made the derogatory comments. After viewing the objectionable video, the Court observed that the continued availability of the video on social media could hurt the religious sentiments of devotees and passed an interim order restricting access to the video. items.title: Karnataka HC calls for implementation of e-notarisation in High Court and district courts
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has directed the Registrar (Judicial), Registrar General and Registrar (Computers) to implement e-notarisation in filings before the Karnataka high Court and the District Court. Justice Suraj Govindaraj directed the acceptance of e-notarisation while taking on record a compliance affidavit that was notarised electronically. The order was passed in a case relating to the restrictions imposed on a bank account pursuant to a cybercrime investigation. Justice Suraj Govindraj Counsel for IIFL Finance Limited, Advocate Priyanka S Bhat, provided a detailed process on how the e-notarisation was obtained in a memorandum of facts filed before the Court. The authorised signatory and notary joined a live audio-video conference with the same affidavit displayed on their screen. The notary verified the signatory's identity and authority to act for the company, confirmed understanding of what was being signed, recorded voluntary participation and administered an oath that the signatory had verified the contents of the affidavit.
